explanation: SOS stands for nothing. It was picked in 1906 because its Morse code, three dots, three dashes and three dots, is easy to send and hard to mistake.

claims.text: SOS was not chosen as an abbreviation of 'Save Our Souls' or 'Save Our Ship'; the letters stand for no words.
SOS was adopted as an international distress signal at the 1906 International Radiotelegraph Convention in Berlin.
In Morse code, SOS is three dots, three dashes and three dots, sent as one continuous signal.
The pattern was chosen because it is easy to send and hard to mistake.
